short: The number of guests served in a period.
metaDescription: A cover is one guest served. Covers separate two very different reasons for a revenue change: fewer guests, or the same guests spending less.
definition: A cover is one guest served. Restaurants count covers per shift, day and month, and use the figure as the denominator for average spend, labour productivity and forecasting.
bodyHtml:
Why Covers matters

Covers separate two very different reasons for a revenue change: fewer guests, or the same guests spending less. The fix is completely different in each case.

Covers formula

Average cover = Total sales ÷ Number of covers

Covers per labour hour is the standard productivity measure.

How Covers works in practice

Record covers per shift alongside sales, so average cover and labour cost per cover can be tracked. Reservation and queue systems capture the count automatically; paper systems rarely do.

faq.question: Is a cover the same as a table?
faq.answer: No. One table of four is four covers.

faq.question: Why track covers if I already track bills?
faq.answer: Bill counts hide party size, so a drop in group bookings looks identical to a drop in walk-ins.
